questions.question: Approximately how many people live outside their country of birth?
options: About 281 million
About 28 million
About 1 billion
About 5 million
questions.explanation: Approximately 281 million people are international migrants — living outside the country where they were born.

questions.question: What is the difference between voluntary and forced migration?
options: Voluntary migrants choose to move; forced migrants flee war, persecution or disaster
Voluntary migration is illegal
Forced migration only happens within a country
There is no difference
questions.explanation: Voluntary migrants move for work, study or family, while forced migrants (refugees) flee danger such as war or persecution.

questions.question: What characterises the "assimilation" model of integration?
options: Newcomers are expected to adopt the host culture and give up their own
Newcomers and hosts adapt to each other
Groups live completely separately
Newcomers keep dual citizenship
questions.explanation: Assimilation expects newcomers to absorb the host culture fully, unlike integration models where adaptation goes both ways.

questions.question: Why are personal stories important when learning about migration?
options: They make abstract statistics human and understandable
They replace the need for facts entirely
They are always more accurate than statistics
They are shorter to read
questions.explanation: Literature and journalism use individual narratives to make the human experience of migration real — beyond the numbers.

questions.question: How does the chapter describe the multiculturalism debate?
options: People of good will hold different views — some emphasise diversity's benefits, others prioritise cohesion
Only one side has valid arguments
The debate was settled decades ago
It is not discussed in English-speaking countries
questions.explanation: The debate involves legitimate different perspectives: some emphasise the benefits of diversity, others prioritise social cohesion.
